title: Daniel Bible Quiz - Chapter 12
description: Ten questions on Daniel 12: Michael standing up, those who sleep in the dust, the sealed book and the counted days.

questions.text: Who will stand up at that time as the great prince who stands for the children of your people?
questions.explanation: The text says that at that time Michael will stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people.

answers.text: Gabriel
Michael
Darius
Daniel

questions.text: In the time of trouble, who does the text say will be delivered?
questions.explanation: The text says that at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.

answers.text: Everyone who fasts and prays
Only the princes of the people
Everyone who flees to the mountains
Everyone who is found written in the book

questions.text: What does the text say about many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth?
questions.explanation: The text says many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

answers.text: They will awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame
They will sleep on until the book is opened
They will be gathered to the glorious land
They will be hidden until the trouble has passed

questions.text: What will those who turn many to righteousness be like, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The text says those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever.

answers.text: They will stand as pillars in the sanctuary
They will be as the sand of the sea
They will shine as the stars forever and ever
They will be hidden in the day of trouble

questions.text: What is Daniel told to do with the words, even to the time of the end?
questions.explanation: The text says Daniel is told to shut up the words and seal the book, even to the time of the end.

answers.text: Read the words aloud to the people
Shut up the words and seal the book
Write the words on the wall of the palace
Carry the book to the king

questions.text: What did Daniel see when he looked, beside the river?
questions.explanation: The text says Daniel looked and saw two others standing, one on the river bank on this side and the other on the river bank on that side.

answers.text: Two others standing, one on each bank of the river
Four chariots coming out from the water
A great beast rising out of the river
A host of horsemen crossing the river

questions.text: What question was put to the man clothed in linen who was above the waters of the river?
questions.explanation: The text says one asked the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, how long it would be to the end of these wonders.

answers.text: Who will stand up for your people?
Where is the book that is sealed?
What is written in the book of truth?
How long will it be to the end of these wonders?

questions.text: What did the man clothed in linen swear that it would be?
questions.explanation: The text says he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven and swore by him who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and a half.

answers.text: For seventy weeks of years
For three full generations
For a time, times, and a half
For a thousand years and more

questions.text: How many days are counted from the taking away of the continual burnt offering and the setting up of the abomination that makes desolate?
questions.explanation: The text says that from the time the continual burnt offering is taken away and the abomination that makes desolate set up, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.

answers.text: One thousand two hundred ninety days
One thousand three hundred thirty-five days
Two thousand three hundred days
Seventy days and seven

questions.text: What is Daniel told at the very end of the chapter?
questions.explanation: The text says Daniel is told to go his way until the end, for he will rest and will stand in his inheritance at the end of the days.

answers.text: To return to the river and wait there
To go his way, for he will rest and stand in his inheritance
To take the book to the king of the north
To tell the people everything he has heard
